# A view loop's copy keeps its state and its lifetimes with its element's
# identity, wherever the list moves it, on every target: the interpreter's
# mounted path, the instance slots of html, fyne and gtk4, bubbletea's cells
# per copy and its settle, and Compose's key. A copy matched by position kept
# the state of whatever element had been at its place, and every copy after a
# dropped one mounted again. Two copies of one identity are two: on bubbletea
# they shared their cells, and an effect under the loop mounted once for both.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +6 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
// A copy of a view loop's body is told from the others by its element's
// identity, and keeps its state while the list holds it, wherever it moves:
// a string, a number or an enum is its own identity, and a struct's is its
// `key()`. A struct with no `key`, and an element bound by `&`, are matched by
// position, and copies sharing one identity by their order among themselves.

import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct todo {
    id    int
    title string

    const func key() => id
}

struct point {
    x int
}

enum shade { light, dark }

var mounts list[string] = []

component counter(label string) ui.node {
    var taps = 0

    effect(@mount { mounts.push(label) })

    ui.button #b(text="{label} {taps}", @click { taps += 1 })
}

component page ui.node {
    var names = ["a", "b", "c"]
    var todos = [todo{id=1, title="x"}, todo{id=2, title="y"}]
    var points = [point{x=1}, point{x=2}]
    var shades = [shade.light, shade.dark]
    var words = ["p", "q"]
    var twins = ["a", "a", "b"]

    ui.vbox {
        for var n = names {
            counter #row(label=n)
        }
        for var t = todos {
            counter #item(label=t.title)
        }
        for var p = points {
            counter #spot(label="{p.x}")
        }
        for var s = shades {
            counter #tint(label="{s}")
        }
        for var &w = words {
            counter #word(label=w)
        }
        for var n = twins {
            counter #twin(label=n)
        }
    }
}

func testACopyFollowsItsString(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.row[1].b.click()
    var before = mounts.length()
    c.names.remove(0)
    t.assert(c.row[0].taps == 1)
    t.assert(c.row[1].taps == 0)
    t.assert(mounts.length() == before)
}

func testACopyFollowsItsKey(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.item[0].b.click()
    c.todos.insert(0, todo{id=3, title="z"})
    t.assert(c.item[0].taps == 0)
    t.assert(c.item[1].taps == 1)
}

func testAKeylessStructIsItsPosition(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.spot[0].b.click()
    c.points.insert(0, point{x=3})
    t.assert(c.spot[0].taps == 1)
    t.assert(c.spot[1].taps == 0)
}

func testACopyFollowsItsMember(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.tint[1].b.click()
    c.shades.remove(0)
    t.assert(c.tint[0].taps == 1)
}

func testTwoCopiesOfOneIdentityAreTwo(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.twin[1].b.click()
    t.assert(c.twin[0].taps == 0)
    t.assert(c.twin[1].taps == 1)
    c.twins.push("a")
    t.assert(c.twin[3].taps == 0)
}

func testARefElementIsItsPosition(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.word[0].b.click()
    c.words.insert(0, "o")
    t.assert(c.word[0].taps == 1)
}

ui.window {
    page
}
